newsitem.title: USA: Fruit of the Loom to sell hosiery business.
newsitem.headline: Fruit of the Loom to sell hosiery business.

text.p: Fruit of the Loom Inc., the nation's largest undergarment maker, said Thursday it agreed to sell a substantial portion of its hosiery manufacturing operations to Renfro Corp.
Renfro is a privately held company based in Mount Airy, N.C., that makes socks sold to leading retailers.
Fruit of the Loom said it expected about $95 million in proceeds from the deal, including working capital items.

In addition, the company granted Renfro an exclusive license to use the Fruit of the Loom trade name and trademark for the manufacture, sale and distribution of athletic, casual and dress socks for adults and children.
The deal is subject to the signing of a definitive purchase agreement and approval by directors of both companies.
The sale involves Fruit of the Loom's plants in Starr, N.C., Whitmire, S.C. and DeKalb, Ala., with about 1,300 employees. The workers are expected to join Renfro.
Fruit of the Loom's stock rose $1.25 to $31.50 on the New York Stock Exchange in early afternoon trading.
